correctness.rationale: The map is a negative-gradient step for the edge cosine potential. Along a lifted step with nonzero gradient g, the Taylor integral is bounded by h²λ||g||²/2; at equality in the step bound h=2/λ, at least one edge difference of g is nonzero and the associated cosine cannot stay at −1 along the step. The strict integral bound establishes strict descent, also ruling out a fixed quotient point with nonzero lifted gradient. Compactness and continuity give the stated periodic/omega-limit consequences, with no assertion of convergence to a single point. Bipartite sign conjugation turns L into an irreducible nonnegative signless Laplacian, so λ is simple; connectedness ensures Q>0. In the antiphase-centered quotient lift, oddness makes f_h(x)=−x the exact centered two-cycle equation. The complement of v is invertible for this equation at criticality, giving w=O(y³) for x=yv+w. The scalar balance is −μy+h_c Qy³/6+O(|μ||y|³+|y|⁵), proving the claimed square-root amplitude and two distinct quotient points. The identical symmetric Jacobians at both points are I−hL+(h/2)BA diag((Bᵀx)²) Bᵀ+O(||x||⁴), with the edge weights included in A. The first-order perturbation of the simple −1 mode is −1−μ+(h/2)Q y²+O(μ²)=−1+2μ+O(μ²), while all transverse eigenvalues remain strictly inside the unit interval. The return derivative is the square, proving attraction on the quotient only. RESULT.md and both support files were inspected; the uploaded script was not run.
